# 채점표 (문제·풀이 공통)

점수 항목(1~5), "이미 알려진 문제", "이해 가능 여부" 항목에는 "판단 불가"를 선택할 수 있다. 확신이 없으면 추측하지 말고 판단 불가를 택한다. 풍요로움은 떠오르는 것이 없으면 비워 두며, 그것이 0점이다.

## 문제 평가
- 명확성 (clarity, 1~5): 1 = 뜻이 통하지 않거나 정의가 빠짐 · 3 = 뜻은 통하지만 모호한 부분이 있음 · 5 = 모든 기호와 조건이 정의되어 한 가지로만 읽힘
- 난이도 (difficulty, 1~5): 1 = 학부 연습문제 수준 · 3 = 대학원생이 며칠 걸릴 수준 · 5 = 현재 알려진 방법으로는 접근이 보이지 않는 수준
- 풍요로움 (richness_list): "이 문제가 풀리면 쉬워지거나 자연스럽게 따라오는 다른 문제"를 생각나는 만큼 적는다. 한 줄에 하나. 없으면 비워 둔다. 점수는 그 개수다.
- 풀고 싶은 정도 (want_to_solve, 1~5): 1 = 전혀 · 3 = 시간이 있으면 · 5 = 지금 바로 붙잡고 싶다
- 이미 알려진 문제 (known_problem, 예/아니오/판단 불가): 이 문제가 이미 알려진 문제·정리와 사실상 같으면 "예".

## 풀이 평가
- 정확성 (correctness, 1~5): 1 = 틀렸거나 핵심 단계가 없음 · 3 = 방향은 맞지만 빈틈이 있음 · 5 = 완전하고 올바름 · 유한 인스턴스가 주어진 문제는 유한 인스턴스에 대한 풀이를 기준으로 평가한다.
- 명료성 (clarity_sol, 1~5): 1 = 따라갈 수 없음 · 3 = 노력하면 따라갈 수 있음 · 5 = 한 번 읽고 따라갈 수 있음
- 이해 가능 여부 (understandable): 이 풀이의 핵심 아이디어를 자기 말로 다시 설명할 수 있으면 "예", 없으면 "아니오", 모르겠으면 "판단 불가"

</rubric>

<problem>
For a Sidon set $S\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ let $S(x)=|S\cap[0,x]|$. Pilatte proved that some Sidon set $S$ is an asymptotic basis of order 3, i.e. every large integer is a sum of three elements of $S$ (repetitions allowed). Is there such a Sidon basis of order 3 with $S(x)\ge x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all large $x$? Equivalently, can a Sidon asymptotic basis of order 3 be almost as dense as the maximal density $\sim x^{1/2}$ of Sidon sets? More generally, determine $\limsup_{x\to\infty}\log S(x)/\log x$ over all Sidon bases of order 3. The trivial bounds are $1/3\le$ this value $\le1/2$.
</problem>

<finite_instance>
Find a Sidon set $S\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,200\}$ with $|S|\le 12$ such that every integer $n$ with $70\le n\le 200$ is a sum of three elements of $S$ (repetitions allowed).
</finite_instance>

<solution>
**Status: I did not solve the finite instance or the general problem.** The candidate below is a near-miss. It is a valid Sidon set, but by my hand computation it misses 8 of the 131 required integers. I had no computer, so all the checks below were done by hand and have not been machine-verified.

**General problem.** I have no new result on whether a Sidon basis of order 3 can have $S(x)\ge x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$, or on the value of the limsup. I can only confirm the trivial bounds:
- Upper bound $1/2$: the differences of elements of $S\cap[0,x]$ are distinct and lie in $[1,x]$, so $S(x)=O(x^{1/2})$.
- Lower bound $1/3$: a basis of order 3 needs $\binom{S(x)+2}{3}\ge x-O(1)$, so $S(x)\gg x^{1/3}$ and the limsup is at least $1/3$.

**Finite instance: construction.** I wrote the set as $S=A\cup B$ with a small part and a large part.
- Take $A=\{0,1,4,10,12,17\}$, a Golomb ruler. Then $T=A+A=\{0,1,2,4,5,8,10,11,12,13,14,16,17,18,20,21,22,24,27,29,34\}$.
- Translates $b+T$ with $b$ differing by about 14 to 19 overlap well, because the holes of $T$ at $3,6,7,9,15,19$ get filled by the neighbouring translate. These sums cover the lower range.
- The sums $b+b'+A$ and $b+b'+b''$ cover the upper range.
- Translating $S$ by $t$ shifts all triple sums by $3t$, so the target window can be slid.

After trying several versions of $B$, the best was $B=\{41,55,73,88,107,130\}$ with $t=1$, which gives
$$S=\{1,2,5,11,13,18,42,56,74,89,108,131\}.$$

**Sidon check.** I listed all pairwise differences for the untranslated set, and they are distinct. They are:
- within $A$: $1,\dots,13,16,17$;
- within $B$: $14,15,18,19,23,32,33,34,42,47,52,57,66,75,89$;
- between $B$ and $A$: $24,29,31,37,38,40,41$, then $43,45,51,54,55,56$, then $61,63,69,71,72,73$, then $76,78,84,87,88,90$, then $95,97,103,106,107$, then $113,118,120,126,129,130$.

**Coverage.** Here $T$ denotes $A+A$ as above, and I checked the untranslated set on the window $[67,197]$, which corresponds to $[70,200]$ after the shift. The sums $B+T$, $B+B+A$ and $B+B+B$ cover everything in the window except the old values $80,103,116,167,168,182,191,194$. For the actual $S$, the integers in $[70,200]$ that I found uncovered are
$$83,\ 106,\ 119,\ 170,\ 171,\ 185,\ 194,\ 197.$$

**Why this set could not be repaired.** With these 11 elements fixed, the Sidon condition rules out any 12th element below $130$, so the low holes cannot be filled that way. Replacing $17$ with nearby values, or moving elements of $B$ (for example $107\to108$, or $B=\{41,56,74,88,109\}$), did not do better. The other designs I tried left at least as many holes, including $A=\{0,1,3,7,12,20\}$ with $B=\{46,62,76,94,109,130\}$, which left 14.

**Final answer.** No valid set was found. The candidate is a Sidon set of size 12 that covers 123 of the 131 integers, so it does **not** satisfy the finite instance. A computer search, such as local search over 12-element Golomb rulers with this $A\cup B$ shape, is the natural next step.
</solution>
